critiques.description: gap-020 records the same unestablished fact as gap-018 and gap-025, and largely as gap-011: evd-001 states that the sync service runs on a virtual machine in the operations subnet and that the kiosks call it over the store network, and names no firewall policy, security group, private link, or service mesh, so which hosts may reach cmp-001 cannot be determined. All four gaps cite the same single passage (evd-001) and the same control (ctl-001), and all four ask for firewall or security-group configuration for the operations subnet. gap-025 already requests the boundary between the store network and the operations subnet, the mechanism that enforces it, and which workloads may reach the submission interface — which is the whole of gap-020's requested evidence. The only item in the set not covered by gap-025 is gap-011's third request, the network origin of the fulfillment system's hourly poll on df-002.
critiques.rationale: One answer — the network policy governing the operations subnet host — closes gap-011, gap-018, gap-020 and gap-025 at once. Left separate, a single silent sentence in service-note.md reads downstream as four distinct verification failures at medium severity each, and puts four near-identical evidence requests in front of the same person. gap-020's own importance statement argues about whether an attacker can 'submit at volume', which is not any step of thr-002's attack path, indicating it was drafted against a different threat's chain and reproduced here on the same passage. Recommend merging gap-018, gap-020 and gap-025 into the broadest formulation (gap-025) and retaining gap-011 only for the distinct df-002 poll-origin question.

critiques.description: Attack path step 1 establishes a 'listening position on the store network path', and step 4 then asserts that 'the same position' permits modifying a record in flight. Those are different capabilities: of the three positions the description names, a tapped port is capture-only, and a compromised device sharing the segment is in-path only after some redirection step; only the rogue access point is inherently in-path. The tampering half of the threat therefore rests on an in-path (active) position that no precondition records. Separately, the impact states the delivery address can be changed 'without either the kiosk or the service seeing an anomaly', which requires that no application-layer integrity or reconciliation check exists on order records. evd-001 says only that the service receives records from the kiosks, stores them, and is polled hourly; it says nothing about record signing, checksums, or confirmation back to the kiosk, so the undetectability claim rests on silence rather than on anything the passage establishes.
critiques.rationale: The disclosure half of this threat is carefully conditioned — three preconditions, each naming what is not established, and low overall confidence. The tampering half is carried by the word 'Optionally' and inherits none of its own conditions, so a downstream reader receives an integrity impact stated more firmly than the disclosure impact it is attached to, with its two enabling conditions never recorded as unknown. Precondition 2's 'readable, or terminable' addresses transport protection, not attacker position, and nothing addresses application-layer integrity at all. Recommend revising to add an in-path-position precondition and an absence-of-integrity-checking precondition (or to split the tampering branch into its own threat); the disclosure analysis and its preconditions need no change.
